target_customer: Clinicians (as pitched on YC) and individual patients with chronic or lifestyle conditions, mainly in the UK and US
problem: Patients with chronic and lifestyle related conditions get little daily support between appointments, and doctors have no easy way to offer it or earn recurring revenue from it.
business_model: Subscription lifestyle medicine programs (12 week protocol, yoga, nutrition, coaching, app) sold to consumers, positioned as a layer for clinicians
product_category: Digital health, lifestyle medicine and complementary care

founders.name: Nived Narayanan
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background given.

founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background given.

founders.name: Amit Kumar Verma
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background given.

technical_complexity.rationale: App plus coaching and clinician service delivery; the difficulty is clinical operations rather than technology.

defensibility.rationale: Programs built from coaching content and services are easy to copy and no data or regulatory moat is evidenced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents copying or buying the offer.

market_need_then: The YC description claims 87 percent of patients improve in weeks; this is a company claim. No independent demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses nirvahealth.com rather than an exact match .com; acquisition details not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Your lifestyle leads. Our plans follow.

rebrands.why: Not stated; former name appears in Trustpilot reviews and CB Insights, both seen only in search results

branding.community_and_virality: Trustpilot reviews exist in many locales; the company claims 50 thousand plus clients (self reported).

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; the name is easily confused with Nirvana Health, a different company that shows up in funding searches.

pivots.from: Lifestyle medicine layer for clinicians (YC pitch)
pivots.to: Direct to consumer UK lifestyle support programs including yoga, Ayurveda and menopause focus
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the YC description versus the current site, so treat as unverified

outcome_analysis: Nirva is still active with about 5 to 10 staff, but no funding round could be verified and no outcome news was found. The product appears to have shifted from a clinician facing layer to consumer programs in the UK. The story is unclear, so factors are left empty rather than guessed.
notes: Unverified: CB Insights shows 500 thousand dollars over 3 rounds (YC, Pioneer Fund, Titan Capital) and says the company was formerly Yara and founded in 2019; this is a single aggregator, not recorded as a round. Search results also surface Nirvana Health, a different company. No dated competitor sources were found for the batch period; CB Insights lists Alvie Health, movr and Morph as current competitors without dates, so they are not recorded. Founder education and employers were not found. Completeness pass: one convertible note dated 2021-01-01 with YC is recorded from CB Insights alone (single database); CB gives only a total of $500K over 3 rounds, so per-round amounts are null and other rounds are missing.
